title: Fix beads helper filtering and auto-commit
description:
dot_local/share/beads-helpers.zsh was added to suppress noisy Beads auto-import messages and auto-commit .beads/issues.jsonl after mutating bd operations, but both behaviors appear broken.

Evidence from a dev container wrapper that invokes bd directly:

```sh
case "$action" in
  status|list|ready|show)
    exec bd --json --readonly "$action" "$@"
    ;;
  create|update)
    exec bd --json "$action" "$@"
    ;;
esac
```

Observed output still includes:

```text
auto-importing 17037 bytes from /workspaces/homelab-IaC/.beads/issues.jsonl into empty database...
auto-imported 17 issues from /workspaces/homelab-IaC/.beads/issues.jsonl
```

After a mutating operation, git status shows .beads/issues.jsonl staged but not committed:

```text
Changes to be committed:
  modified:   .beads/issues.jsonl
```

This definitely occurs in the dev container and likely also occurs on the host.
acceptance_criteria:
- auto-import status messages are filtered in the dev container workflow.
- Mutating bd operations refresh and commit .beads/issues.jsonl when auto-commit is enabled.
- Read-only bd operations do not attempt export or git commits.
- The behavior is validated on host or with a reproducible dev-container-equivalent path.

comments.author: Balaji Dutt
comments.text: Reproduced on host while creating this tracking issue: running `bd create --json ...` printed the auto-importing/auto-imported messages for /Users/balaji/Documents/development/dotfiles/.beads/issues.jsonl, and .beads/issues.jsonl remained modified instead of being auto-committed. This confirms the host path is affected too, not only the dev container.

Split container-dotfiles into a separate (submodule) repository
description:
## Migration steps

### A. Extract history & create the new repo

1. Pre-flight (clean tree). Capture golden render references:
   - `chezmoi execute-template --file private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles/devcontainers/gitlab.com/servers-homelab/homelab-IaC/dot_devcontainer/devcontainer.json.tmpl > /tmp/golden-devcontainer.json`
   - same for `dotfiles/dot_gitconfig.tmpl` and `dotfiles/dot_local/bin/executable_opencode-plannotator{,-custom}.tmpl`.
   - `chezmoi target-path private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles/dotfiles/dot_zshrc` (record output).
2. In a scratch clone of core:
   `git subtree split --prefix=private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles -b export/container-dotfiles`
3. Create public GitLab repo `balaji-personal-files/container-dotfiles`; push
   `export/container-dotfiles` as its `main`.
4. In the new repo add: `.gitignore` containing `dotfiles/configs/` (rendered
   secrets — must never be committed there) and a short `README.md`.

### B. Wire submodule into core

5. `git rm -r private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles` (commit).
6. `git submodule add git@gitlab.com:balaji-personal-files/container-dotfiles.git private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles`
   (creates `.gitmodules` + gitlink at the identical path).
7. Verify rendering parity (see Verification) **before** any other edit.

### C. Core repo adjustments (minimal — paths are unchanged)

Critical files (all repo-relative paths unchanged because the submodule sits at
the same location — most edits are guards/comments/docs, not path rewrites):

- **`.chezmoiignore`** — no path edits (lines 64-67 OS gate; 153-154 rendered
  configs ignore stay valid). Verify `.gitmodules`/submodule `.git` are not
  surfaced as managed targets; add an ignore only if needed.
- **`assets/sync-devcontainer-assets.sh`**, **`assets/sync-opencode-copilot-profiles.sh`**,
  **`assets/sync-devcontainer-all.sh`**, **`assets/render-container-configs.sh`** —
  add a preamble guard: if `private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles/.git`
  is absent, fail loudly with `git submodule update --init --recursive` hint
  (prevents silently writing untracked files into an empty submodule dir).
- **`configs/devcontainer-sync.jsonc`** — no path edits (all `*_root` repo-relative);
  add a comment noting `target_root` now lands in a submodule working tree.
- **`bin/executable_sync-devcontainer-all.sh.tmpl`** — unchanged; optional
  submodule-init hint.
- **3 chezmoi hooks** — verify, expect no functional edits:
  - `.chezmoiscripts/run_after_50-publish-devcontainer-overlays-wsl.sh.tmpl`
    (`$SOURCE_DIR/private_Documents/.../devcontainers/**/devcontainer.json.tmpl`
    now resolves into the submodule — still found).
  - `.chezmoiscripts/run_once_after_99-cleanup-wrong-apply.sh.tmpl` (operates on
    destination `~/Documents/...` — unaffected).
  - `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_devcontainer_sync_reminder.sh.tmpl` (and
    sibling onchange reminders) — `include`s read files from disk; add a
    submodule-init fallback message.
- **Bootstrap** — add `git submodule update --init --recursive` to
  `bootstrap-wsl.sh` (and the macOS bootstrap path) before first `chezmoi apply`.
- **Docs** — `docs/devcontainers.md` (Build-Time Sync Model + Platform Behavior:
  document the new repo, submodule init/update, the 2-commit sync flow, rendering
  model unchanged) and `docs/variables.md` (note data vars still feed the
  submodule's templates via outer chezmoi).
- **`devcontainer.json.tmpl` mounts** — **no edits**; re-render and diff vs golden.

### D. Audit & commit (per repo policy)

For every changed core file run `./assets/cz-audit.sh check <repo-relative-path>`.
`.chezmoiignore`/`.gitmodules` are special — use the audit tool only (no direct
`chezmoi apply --dry-run`). Then `chezmoi doctor` (vault/“config template
changed” warnings ignorable). Commit core changes (50/72 format, full-format
since multi-file/new-file); commit the container repo separately; bump+commit the
submodule pointer in core last. `docs/*` follow normal commit (not in the
reviewed-docs gate).
design:
## Context

The core dotfiles repo (`git@gitlab.com:balaji-personal-files/dotfiles.git`, public)
carries a large `private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles/**` subtree
(~112 files, ~184 commits) that drives the homelab-IaC devcontainer and all
container-side dotfiles. It bloats the core repo and churns it with
devcontainer-only changes.

Goal: move that subtree into its own repo to de-bloat core, while **fully
preserving** today's behaviour — chezmoi still renders the moved `.tmpl` files
with host prompt/data context, the host->container sync still works, and the
devcontainer mounts are unchanged.

Verified mechanic that drives the design: there is **no `.chezmoiroot` and no
nested chezmoi**. The OUTER chezmoi attribute-translates and `.tmpl`-renders the
subtree (e.g. `private_Documents/.../dotfiles/dot_zshrc` →
`~/Documents/development/container-dotfiles/dotfiles/.zshrc`; `devcontainer.json.tmpl`
consumes `.CERTFILES_RAW`, `.CERTPATH`, `.plannotator_ports.*`, `.homelab.*`,
`.chezmoi.os/.homeDir`; `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` uses `.name` + `onepasswordRead`).
The container then just `rsync`/`cp`s the *applied* tree — no second chezmoi.

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- **Wiring:** Git **submodule** at the same path `private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles/`.
- **History:** Preserve via `git subtree split` (no new tooling).
- **New repo visibility:** **Public** — `git@gitlab.com:balaji-personal-files/container-dotfiles.git`.

Rationale for submodule: a submodule checkout is just files on disk, so the
outer chezmoi keeps rendering them exactly as today — **zero** template, mount,
data-variable, or rendering-model changes. The sync/orchestration scripts and
chezmoi data stay in core (they need core prompts/`.chezmoidata.yaml`/1Password).
Accepted cost: submodule init/update per machine, and a 2-commit flow when sync
writes into the submodule (commit in submodule, then bump pointer in core).
acceptance_criteria:
1. **Attribute translation intact:** `chezmoi target-path private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles/dotfiles/dot_zshrc`
   equals the pre-migration value; spot-check `dot_gitconfig.tmpl`,
   `private_dot_config/opencode`, `dot_devcontainer/devcontainer.json.tmpl`.
2. **Render parity:** re-run the `chezmoi execute-template --file ...` commands
   from step 1 and `diff` against `/tmp/golden-*` — expect zero diff.
3. **Audit:** `./assets/cz-audit.sh check <path>` clean for each changed file.
4. **Dry apply:** on macOS/Debian-WSL2 `chezmoi diff Documents/development/container-dotfiles`
   + `chezmoi apply --dry-run --verbose` — no spurious diffs. On this Ubuntu-WSL2
   box confirm `chezmoi ignored | grep container-dotfiles` still lists it.
5. **Sync round-trip:** `git submodule update --init`; run `assets/sync-devcontainer-all.sh`;
   `git -C private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles status` shows changes
   only inside the submodule; re-run → idempotent ("no changes").
6. **Overlay-publish (Debian-WSL2):** manually run the
   `chezmoi execute-template --file "$tmpl"` line from the publish hook; `cmp`
   against the pre-migration `personal-wsl/devcontainer.json` — identical.
7. **Negative check:** with submodule *uninitialized*, sync scripts fail loudly
   with the init hint (guard from step C) rather than creating untracked files.
8. `chezmoi doctor` clean; `.gitmodules` not a managed target.

## Rollback

Revert the core commits (submodule remove + re-add the subtree from
`git rm` parent), or `git submodule deinit` and restore the deleted tree from
history. The new repo can be left in place (harmless) or deleted.

title: Determine if assets/sync-opencode-copilot-profiles.sh can be removed
description:
So assets/sync-opencode-copilot-profiles.sh regenerates the static Copilot profile from the main OpenCode config, keeping selected hand-authored agent entries and mapping OpenAI-backed agents to GitHub Copilot equivalents.
   That said, after the new runtime merge work, there is some overlap:
   - sync-opencode-copilot-profiles.sh creates/updates the checked-in profiles/copilot/opencode.jsonc.
   - opencode-sync-workspace-overrides.sh also remaps OpenAI models at runtime when copilot is active.
   So the Copilot profile generator is partly historical and partly useful as a checked-in/fallback artifact. The runtime helper is now the main thing that makes stacked profiles work.
   My honest take: the current behavior is correct, but the naming/flow is confusing. A future cleanup could either:
   1. keep the Copilot generator but document it as “derive checked-in Copilot profile from base config”, or
   2. remove most of the generated Copilot profile and rely fully on runtime remapping.
   I would not remove it casually in this change because it may still serve as fallback/static profile behavior, but it is a reasonable simplification target.

sync-devcontainer-assets.sh reports inaccurate synced-file count
description:
`assets/sync-devcontainer-assets.sh` (invoked via `assets/sync-devcontainer-all.sh` or `~/bin/sync-devcontainer-all.sh`) reports `synced 0 file(s)` on the run that actually performs the copy, then reports the accurate count on the next run.

## Observed sequence

Reproduced during the env-var work on branch `feat-update-claude-code-config` (commits 45d31da and 171eb39):

1. Edited `dot_claude/private_settings.json` in feature worktree (drift fix: statusLine key reorder + trailing newline strip).
2. Ran `~/bin/sync-devcontainer-all.sh` (launcher hardcodes main checkout as `repo_root`). Sync compared MAIN worktree source to container — matched — reported `claude-user-config: synced 0 file(s)`. Correct, but feature-worktree changes weren't propagated.
3. Ran `bash assets/sync-devcontainer-all.sh` directly from the feature worktree. Sync compared feature source to container — differed — but still reported `claude-user-config: synced 0 file(s)`. `git status` afterwards showed the container file modified, and `diff host container` returned exit 0. So the copy DID happen, but the count was wrong.
4. Later, after adding env vars to the host source, a third sync reported `claude-user-config: synced 1 file(s)` correctly.

## Hypothesis

The counter probably fires on a comparison/state branch that doesn't match the actual copy branch. Possibly a stat/hash cache issue, or the counter increments only when the target file's mtime differs from a tracked value rather than when bytes differ.

## Suggested next steps

- Read `assets/sync-devcontainer-assets.sh` mirror loop and inspect where the `synced N file(s)` counter is incremented vs. where files are actually written.
- Check whether the python sync uses `shutil.copy2` (preserves mtime) and compares mtime rather than content for the count.
- Add a regression test that asserts the count matches actual copies.

## Tangential observation

The launcher template at `bin/executable_sync-devcontainer-all.sh.tmpl` hardcodes `repo_root="{{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}/Documents/development/dotfiles"`, which means `~/bin/sync-devcontainer-all.sh` can't sync changes from a feature worktree. Workaround is to invoke the asset script directly via `bash assets/sync-devcontainer-all.sh` from the worktree. Not strictly the same bug, but related to the same workflow.

title: Harden new skills against shell quirks (noclobber, cwd persistence)
description:
Two latent issues surfaced by dotfiles-reviewer during the worktree-merge
E2E review (commit d795f74) but not blocking enough to roll into that
fix.

## Nit 1 — beads-work Step 4 uses a `>` redirect

The state-file write at `dot_claude/skills/beads-work/SKILL.md` Step 4
uses `cat > .beads/in-progress-claude.json <<JSON ...`. Under zsh
`noclobber` this would refuse to overwrite an existing file -- exactly
the bug `bd export -o` was just fixed for in Step 12.

Today this is masked because the state file is always removed in Step
12 or the release sequence, and the "conflicting state file" edge case
asks the user before overwriting. But the asymmetric handling is the
hazard: a future agent could regress this without noticing. Replace
the heredoc redirect with either `>|` (POSIX clobber override, works in
both bash and zsh) or `rm -f .beads/in-progress-claude.json &&
cat > ... <<JSON`.

## Nit 2 — worktree-merge Steps 4-7 lack cwd reminders

`dot_claude/skills/worktree-merge/SKILL.md` Step 3 now carries a clear
warning that cwd does not persist across Bash calls and that each
subsequent step needs its own `cd "\$MAIN_WT"`. But Steps 4, 5, 6, 7
still show bare `git status`, `git fetch`, `git merge --ff-only`,
`git merge --no-ff`, `git log` commands without a `cd "\$MAIN_WT" &&`
prefix. An agent skimming the skill could miss the Step 3 warning and
re-introduce the bug.

Add a one-line "Re-issue `cd \"\$MAIN_WT\"` first" reminder at the top
of Steps 4, 5, 6, and 7 (or wrap the sample commands themselves in
`cd "\$MAIN_WT" && ...` chains).

## Files

- dot_claude/skills/beads-work/SKILL.md (Step 4)
- dot_claude/skills/worktree-merge/SKILL.md (Steps 4-7)
- Mirror to private_dot_config/opencode/skills/... + container-dotfiles
- Run ./assets/cz-audit.sh check on each
- Run ./assets/sync-devcontainer-all.sh

## Related

Both nits called out in the dotfiles-reviewer pass over commit d795f74.
acceptance_criteria: beads-work Step 4 uses a noclobber-safe write for the state file; worktree-merge Steps 4-7 carry a 'cd $MAIN_WT first' reminder; both fixes mirrored to OpenCode + container-dotfiles; cz-audit clean.

comments.text:
## Nit 3 — `git show-ref*` allowlist entry is redundant

Surfaced by dotfiles-reviewer pass on commit cce5d2a.

The new `private_dot_config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` line `"git show-ref*": "allow"` is already covered by the pre-existing `"git show*": "allow"` pattern, since OpenCode uses prefix-style matching with `last-matching-rule-wins` and both evaluate to allow. The entry has no behavioral effect today.

Two options:

1. **Leave as defensive documentation** with a clarifying comment, e.g.
   `"git show-ref*": "allow",  // explicit for worktree-merge (already covered by "git show*")`
   Useful if someone later restricts `git show*` to `ask` (e.g. for large-output reasons) so ref inspection stays allowed.

2. **Remove** as dead config from both:
   - `private_dot_config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`
   - `private_Documents/development/container-dotfiles/dotfiles/private_dot_config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`

Mr. Dutt to decide as part of resolving dots-91t.

Same fix-cycle as Nit 1 and Nit 2: edit both files, run `./assets/cz-audit.sh check`, mirror is host-only-no-mirror so no `sync-devcontainer-all.sh` needed.
